newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare losses, but still end lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare losses, but still end lower.

text.p: German shares ended a turbulent day of trading on Friday lower in electronic trade as Wall Street opened lower despite having earlier hit an all-time record close in Frankfurt bourse trade.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures all-day electronic trade in German shares, came off earlier lows to end the day at 2,915.81 points, down 20.88 points or 0.71 percent.
Evidence of the see-saw nature of the day's trade lay in the fact that the DAX-30 index earlier ended bourse trade at a record 2,933.39 points, up 40.76 points or 1.41 percent higher.
Higher-than-expected U.S. jobless data dragged the IBIS DAX index lower in early afternoon, and losses were compounded by a nearly one-percent lower opening on the Dow Jones Index on Wall Street.
"This intraday volatility on Wall Street is a nightmare," said one trader. However, the dollar stayed strong and so support at 2,900 points held firm.
Dealers were looking ahead to a rash of U.S. data next week for inspiration to bring the index higher again.

The main share in the news was the carmaker Volkswagen AG, which rose earlier in the session but ended the day down 4.40 marks at 703.50 marks in line with the market and on profit-taking after hefty gains this week.
The carmaker reached an out-of-court settlement late on Thursday with General Motors Corp over allegations of industrial spying when VW hired away a top GM manager in 1993.

Utilities were also favoured over the course of the day and the three largest all ended higher against the run of play. Veba AG finished up 40 pfennigs at 92.30 marks, Viag AG ended up one mark at 644 and RWE AG ended up 32 pfennigs at 66.64.
